safety_line: Roaches can carry bacteria picked up outdoors. Wash hands after cleanup and keep food covered.
traits: Reddish-brown, 1.5-2 inches long, with a pale yellowish band behind the head
Can glide-fly, usually from a high spot toward light
Wanders in from mulch, palms, and drains, especially after heavy rain or drought
The largest common roach found in Florida homes

look_alikes.difference: American cockroaches have a pale band behind the head; smokybrown cockroaches are uniformly dark mahogany with no band.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up from above of the area right behind the head.

copy.what_it_means: The classic Florida "palmetto bug" lives outdoors in mulch, palms, and sewers — one indoors is usually a visitor, not an infestation. Occasional wanderers are weather-driven; nightly sightings point to an entry point or moisture source worth fixing.
copy.fact: It lives outdoors in mulch, palms, and sewers — one in the house is a visitor, not necessarily an infestation.
copy.blurb: The classic Florida "palmetto bug" — a large outdoor roach that wanders inside from mulch, palms, and drains. Occasional sightings are usually weather-driven; frequent ones point to an entry point or moisture source worth checking.

tech_notes: Reddish, yellow pronotum band, strong flier. Source: mulch beds, palm boots, sewer/drain lines. Exterior-first program + dewebbing entry points.

traits: Uniform dark mahogany-to-black, no light band behind the head
About 1 to 1.25 inches, strong flier drawn to porch lights
Favors gutters, tree holes, and attics — needs consistent moisture
Wings extend past the abdomen in both sexes

look_alikes.difference: Smokybrown cockroaches are uniformly dark with no band behind the head; American cockroaches have a pale yellow band there.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up from above of the area right behind the head.

copy.what_it_means: Smokybrown cockroaches follow moisture, so clogged gutters and damp attics are a favorite address. Porch-light visitors are normal; regular attic activity is worth addressing.
copy.fact: It dries out easily, so it follows moisture — clogged gutters are a favorite address for this one.
copy.blurb: Dries out easily, so it follows moisture — clogged gutters are a favorite address.

tech_notes: Uniform dark mahogany, strong flier. Check gutters, soffit vents, attic moisture. Exterior perimeter + attic inspection if recurring.

safety_line: German roach infestations can trigger allergies and asthma and can adulterate food with feces and shed skins. Keep food sealed and surfaces clean while treatment is underway.
traits: Small, tan, with two dark parallel racing stripes behind the head
Found near appliances, under sinks, and in cabinet hinges
Rarely survives outdoors in Florida — arrives via bags, boxes, or used appliances
Seeing them in daylight often suggests a heavy, established population

look_alikes.difference: German cockroaches have two straight parallel stripes on the pronotum; brown-banded cockroaches have bands across the wings and a more mottled look.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up from above of the stripe or band pattern, next to a coin.

copy.what_it_means: German roaches breed indoors — kitchens and bathrooms — and multiply fast with overlapping generations. A technician typically starts with an inspection to scope a cleanout approach suited to how far it's spread.
copy.fact: This species rarely lives outdoors in Florida — it arrives in bags, boxes, and used appliances. It's a hitchhiker, not a cleanliness verdict.
copy.blurb: German roaches breed indoors — kitchens and bathrooms — and multiply fast. Worth having looked at quickly; a technician scopes a cleanout after inspecting the extent.

tech_notes: Two pronotum stripes, nymphs banded. Gel bait + IGR cleanout, no repellents. Grade infestation level for cleanout scope — quote after inspection.
